subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The Fur Trade and Its Impact on Indigenous Peoples and Settlers
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: the fur trade was an early economic system in Canada built on the exchange of furs, which relied heavily on partnerships and knowledge shared between Indigenous peoples and European settlers.

quiz.q: The fur trade was primarily built on the exchange of ___.
options: Furs, especially beaver pelts, for goods
A concept unrelated to the fur trade
Modern currency for stocks
Land for gold

quiz.q: The fur trade relied heavily on partnerships between ___.
options: Indigenous peoples and European settlers
Groups with no connection to trade at all
Only European countries with each other
A concept unrelated to the fur trade

quiz.q: Which skill did Indigenous peoples often contribute to the success of the fur trade?
options: No useful skills or knowledge at all
A concept unrelated to the fur trade
Knowledge of the land and trapping techniques
Knowledge of overseas shipping routes only

quiz.q: Why did the fur trade have such a significant impact on early Canada?
options: The fur trade only affected European countries directly
The fur trade had no effect on Canada’s early development
It shaped economic relationships, exploration, and settlement patterns
A reason unrelated to the fur trade

quiz.q: Why do historians study the fur trade today?
options: It helps explain early relationships between Indigenous peoples and European settlers
The fur trade never actually took place in Canada
The fur trade has no historical significance
A reason unrelated to Canadian history

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Writing: Writing a Business Letter of Complaint or Request
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: a business letter of complaint or request uses formal language and a clear structure to address an issue or ask for action from a company or organization.

quiz.q: A business letter of complaint should use ___.
options: Casual slang and abbreviations
Formal, polite, and clear language
No greeting or closing at all
A concept unrelated to business letters

quiz.q: Which is an appropriate opening for a business letter?
options: A greeting unrelated to formal letters
Hey there!
Yo,
Dear Customer Service Manager,

quiz.q: A letter of complaint should clearly state ___.
options: Only compliments about the company
The problem and what resolution is being requested
A concept unrelated to letters of complaint
Nothing specific at all

quiz.q: Which closing is appropriate for a formal business letter?
options: A closing unrelated to formal letters
Later,
Sincerely,
See ya,

quiz.q: Why is a clear, specific description of the problem important in a complaint letter?
options: Vague complaints are always more effective
A reason unrelated to letter writing
Specific details only confuse the reader
It helps the reader understand exactly what needs to be fixed

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions and Mixed Numbers
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: multiplying fractions involves multiplying numerators and denominators directly, while dividing fractions involves multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor.

quiz.q: To multiply two fractions, you ___.
options: Multiply the numerators together and the denominators together
Find a common denominator first
A concept unrelated to multiplying fractions
Add the numerators together

quiz.q: What is 1/2 x 2/3?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: To divide by a fraction, you multiply by its ___.
options: A concept unrelated to dividing fractions
Reciprocal
Denominator squared
Numerator only

quiz.q: What is 3/4 ÷ 1/2?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: How do you convert a mixed number like 2 1/3 into an improper fraction?
options: Multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator
A method unrelated to mixed numbers
Add the whole number and denominator together
Multiply the whole number by the numerator only

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Volcanoes and Earthquakes: Causes and Effects
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: volcanoes and earthquakes are often caused by the movement of tectonic plates, releasing built-up pressure and energy that can dramatically reshape the Earth’s surface.

quiz.q: Volcanoes and earthquakes are often caused by ___.
options: A concept unrelated to volcanoes and earthquakes
Changes in the moon’s orbit
The movement of tectonic plates
A sudden increase in ocean temperature

quiz.q: An earthquake occurs when ___.
options: A concept unrelated to earthquakes
Built-up pressure along a fault is suddenly released
The Earth’s surface remains perfectly still
Ocean currents shift direction

quiz.q: A volcano erupts when ___.
options: A concept unrelated to volcanic eruptions
Water evaporates from the ocean
Magma and gases escape from beneath the Earth’s surface
The Earth’s crust cools and hardens completely

quiz.q: Which of these regions is most likely to experience frequent earthquakes and volcanic activity?
options: A region unrelated to plate boundaries
An area with no connection to plate boundaries at all
An area located far from any plate boundary
An area located along a tectonic plate boundary

quiz.q: Why do scientists monitor volcanoes and fault lines?
options: To help predict potential eruptions or earthquakes and protect nearby communities
A reason unrelated to Earth science
Volcanoes and fault lines never pose any risk to communities
Monitoring these areas provides no useful information

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The War of 1812: Causes and Consequences
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: the War of 1812 was fought between the United States and Britain (with its colonies, including present-day Canada), shaping early Canadian identity and border relations.

quiz.q: The War of 1812 was fought between the United States and ___.
options: France, alone, with no other countries involved
Spain, alone, with no other countries involved
A country unrelated to the War of 1812
Britain, including its colonies such as present-day Canada

quiz.q: Which of these was a cause of the War of 1812?
options: Trade restrictions and disputes over territory and shipping rights
A complete absence of any tension between the countries
A cause unrelated to the War of 1812
A disagreement about a sporting event

quiz.q: How did the War of 1812 affect the identity of early Canadians?
options: It helped strengthen a shared sense of identity in defending their homeland
A reason unrelated to Canadian identity
It had no effect on how Canadians viewed themselves
It caused Canada to become part of the United States

quiz.q: Which of these was a result of the War of 1812?
options: All trade between the two nations ended permanently
The border between the United States and British North America remained largely unchanged
A result unrelated to the War of 1812
The United States gained full control over all of British North America

quiz.q: Why is the War of 1812 an important event in Canadian history?
options: It played a role in shaping early Canadian identity and relations with the United States
The war had no lasting effects of any kind
The War of 1812 has no connection to Canadian history
A reason unrelated to its historical significance

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Grammar: Correcting Run-on Sentences and Comma Splices
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: a run-on sentence incorrectly joins two independent clauses with no punctuation, while a comma splice incorrectly joins them with only a comma; both can be fixed with a period, semicolon, or conjunction.

quiz.q: A run-on sentence occurs when ___.
options: A sentence has only one clause
A concept unrelated to run-on sentences
Two independent clauses are joined with no punctuation
A sentence is too short to make sense

quiz.q: A comma splice occurs when ___.
options: A sentence uses too many commas correctly
Two independent clauses are joined by only a comma
A concept unrelated to comma splices
A sentence has no clauses at all

quiz.q: Which is a correct way to fix a comma splice?
options: Remove all punctuation from the sentence
A method unrelated to fixing comma splices
Add another comma splice
Replace the comma with a semicolon or add a conjunction

quiz.q: Which sentence is a run-on?
options: I finished my homework I went outside to play
I finished my homework, and I went outside to play.
I finished my homework before I went outside.
A sentence unrelated to run-ons

quiz.q: Why is it important to fix run-on sentences and comma splices?
options: A reason unrelated to grammar
Run-on sentences are always the correct way to write
These errors never affect a reader’s understanding
They can confuse readers about where one idea ends and another begins

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Order of Operations with Integers and Exponents (BEDMAS Deeper Dive)
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: the order of operations (BEDMAS) determines the sequence for evaluating expressions with brackets, exponents, division, multiplication, addition, and subtraction, including those with integers.

quiz.q: BEDMAS stands for the order: ___.
options: Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division
An order unrelated to BEDMAS
Brackets, Exponents, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction
Exponents, Brackets, Subtraction, Addition

quiz.q: Evaluate: 3 + 4 x 2.
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Evaluate: (2 + 3)².
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Evaluate: -2 + (-3) x 2.
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why must operations be completed in a specific order?
options: Order of operations never affects the result of a calculation
Expressions can be solved in any order with the same result
Without a consistent order, the same expression could give multiple different, incorrect answers
A reason unrelated to BEDMAS

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Magnetism and Electromagnets
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: magnetism is a force that attracts certain materials, such as iron, and an electromagnet is a temporary magnet created when electric current flows through a coiled wire.

quiz.q: Magnetism is a force that attracts materials such as ___.
options: Plastic
Iron
A material unrelated to magnetism
Wood

quiz.q: An electromagnet is created when ___.
options: A permanent magnet is placed in water
A concept unrelated to electromagnets
A material is heated to a very high temperature
Electric current flows through a coiled wire

quiz.q: Unlike a permanent magnet, an electromagnet’s magnetism can be ___.
options: Increased only by cooling it down
Never changed once created
Turned on and off by controlling the electric current
A concept unrelated to electromagnets

quiz.q: Which of these could increase the strength of an electromagnet?
options: Removing the electric current entirely
Using a material that does not conduct electricity
A concept unrelated to electromagnets
Increasing the number of coils of wire

quiz.q: Why are electromagnets useful in devices like electric motors and doorbells?
options: A reason unrelated to electromagnets
Their magnetism can be controlled and adjusted using electricity
Electromagnets cannot be used in any electrical device
Electromagnets provide no practical use in technology

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: The Red River Resistance and Louis Riel
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: the Red River Resistance was led by Louis Riel and the Métis people to protect their land, rights, and way of life as Canada expanded westward in the late 1800s.

quiz.q: The Red River Resistance was led by ___.
options: A group with no connection to the Métis
Louis Riel and the Métis people
A group unrelated to the Red River Resistance
A group opposed to protecting any land rights

quiz.q: The Red River Resistance occurred largely in response to ___.
options: An unrelated international conflict
Canada’s westward expansion threatening Métis land and rights
A cause unrelated to the Red River Resistance
A sudden decrease in Canada’s population

quiz.q: The Métis people are often described as having ___.
options: Ancestry unrelated to Canadian history
Mixed Indigenous and European ancestry
Ancestry entirely unrelated to Canada’s history
No connection to Indigenous or European heritage

quiz.q: Why is Louis Riel considered a significant figure in Canadian history?
options: He led efforts to protect Métis rights and land during a period of major change
He opposed all forms of Métis representation
A reason unrelated to his historical significance
He played no role in Canadian history

quiz.q: Why do students study the Red River Resistance today?
options: It highlights the struggles for Indigenous and Métis rights during Canada’s expansion
This event has no connection to understanding Canadian history
A reason unrelated to social studies learning
The Red River Resistance never actually took place

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Vocabulary: Homophones and Homographs
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: homophones are words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings, while homographs are spelled the same but may have different meanings and pronunciations.

quiz.q: Homophones are words that ___.
options: Have the exact same meaning as one another
Are spelled identically but sound different
A concept unrelated to homophones
Sound alike but have different meanings and spellings

quiz.q: Which pair of words are homophones?
options: Run and jog
Happy and sad
There and their
A pair unrelated to homophones

quiz.q: A homograph is a word that ___.
options: Always sounds completely different from other words
A concept unrelated to homographs
Has only one possible meaning
Is spelled the same as another word but may differ in meaning or pronunciation

quiz.q: Which word is a homograph, having two different pronunciations and meanings?
options: A pair unrelated to homographs
Lead (to guide) and lead (the metal)
Cat and dog
Happy and joyful

quiz.q: Why can homophones be tricky for writers?
options: Homophones are always spelled identically
Homophones never cause any confusion in writing
A reason unrelated to vocabulary
They are easy to confuse because they sound the same but are spelled differently

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Volume and Surface Area of Pyramids and Cones
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: the volume of a pyramid or cone is one-third the volume of a prism or cylinder with the same base and height, and their surface area includes the base plus the slanted lateral surface.

quiz.q: The volume of a pyramid or cone is ___ the volume of a prism or cylinder with the same base and height.
options: Three times
A fraction unrelated to this relationship
One-third
Exactly the same as

quiz.q: The formula for the volume of a cone is ___.
options: 2πrh
A formula unrelated to the volume of a cone
πr²h
(1/3)πr²h

quiz.q: The surface area of a pyramid includes ___.
options: Only the base, with no other surfaces
A concept unrelated to surface area
Only the height of the pyramid
The base plus the area of its triangular faces

quiz.q: If a cone and a cylinder share the same base and height, and the cylinder’s volume is 90 cm³, what is the cone’s volume?
options: 30 cm³
90 cm³
270 cm³
A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why might understanding cone and pyramid volume be useful in real life?
options: It helps calculate the capacity of objects like ice cream cones or tents
These calculations have no real-world use
Cones and pyramids never have a measurable volume
A reason unrelated to volume

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Greenhouse Effect and Global Climate Change
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: the greenhouse effect occurs when gases in the atmosphere trap heat from the sun, and an increase in these gases from human activity is linked to global climate change.

quiz.q: The greenhouse effect occurs when gases in the atmosphere ___.
options: Trap heat from the sun near the Earth’s surface
A concept unrelated to the greenhouse effect
Block all sunlight from reaching the Earth
Remove all heat from the atmosphere

quiz.q: Which of these is considered a greenhouse gas?
options: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Oxygen
A gas unrelated to the greenhouse effect

quiz.q: Which human activity is commonly linked to increased greenhouse gas emissions?
options: Burning fossil fuels
Drinking water
Planting large numbers of trees
An activity unrelated to greenhouse gases

quiz.q: A natural greenhouse effect is important because it ___.
options: A reason unrelated to the greenhouse effect
Has no effect on Earth’s temperature
Keeps the Earth warm enough to support life
Makes the Earth too cold to support life

quiz.q: Why are scientists concerned about an increase in greenhouse gases from human activity?
options: Increased greenhouse gases have no effect on global temperatures
Greenhouse gases only affect a single, isolated location
A reason unrelated to climate change
It can lead to rising global temperatures and significant climate changes

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Canada’s Territorial Evolution: How the Provinces and Territories Joined
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: Canada’s provinces and territories joined Confederation at different times, gradually expanding the country’s borders from the original four provinces in 1867 to the ten provinces and three territories of today.

quiz.q: Canada began Confederation in 1867 with how many original provinces?
options: A number unrelated to Confederation
Ten
Thirteen
Four

quiz.q: Canada’s territorial evolution refers to ___.
options: A concept unrelated to Canada’s territorial evolution
How provinces and territories gradually joined the country over time
A single event where all provinces joined at once
A process unrelated to Canada’s formation

quiz.q: Why might a region have chosen to join Confederation?
options: Regions were required to remain isolated forever
No benefit was ever offered to any region
Economic, political, or security benefits of joining a larger country
A reason unrelated to Confederation

quiz.q: How many provinces and territories make up Canada today?
options: Four provinces and no territories
A number unrelated to Canada today
Ten provinces and three territories
Twenty provinces and five territories

quiz.q: Why is it useful to study how Canada’s provinces and territories joined over time?
options: It helps explain the country’s political development and regional differences
This history has no connection to understanding Canada today
Canada’s borders have never changed since 1867
A reason unrelated to social studies learning

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing Internal and External Conflict
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: internal conflict is a struggle within a character’s own mind, while external conflict is a struggle between a character and an outside force, such as another character or nature.

quiz.q: Internal conflict is a struggle ___.
options: Between two separate characters
Within a character’s own mind

quiz.q: External conflict is a struggle between a character and ___.
options: An outside force, such as another character or nature
Only their own thoughts and feelings
A concept unrelated to external conflict
Nothing at all

quiz.q: Which is an example of internal conflict?
options: A character struggling to decide between telling the truth or a lie
A character fighting against a storm at sea
A concept unrelated to internal conflict

quiz.q: Which is an example of external conflict?
options: A character reflecting quietly alone
A concept unrelated to external conflict
A character competing against a rival in a race
A character silently doubting their own abilities

quiz.q: Why might an author include both internal and external conflict in a story?
options: A reason unrelated to narrative writing

Stories are always more interesting with no conflict at all

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Probability: Combinations and Permutations (Intro)
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: a permutation counts the number of ways items can be arranged when order matters, while a combination counts the number of ways items can be selected when order does not matter.

quiz.q: A permutation counts arrangements where ___.

options: A value unrelated to the calculation

Combination

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Density and Buoyancy
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: density is the amount of mass in a given volume of a substance, and buoyancy explains why objects less dense than a fluid float while denser objects sink.

quiz.q: Density is defined as ___.

quiz.q: An object will float in water if it is ___.
options: A concept unrelated to buoyancy

options: Less dense than water

options: Mass multiplied by temperature

A formula unrelated to density

quiz.q: Why can a large steel ship float, even though steel is denser than water?
options: Ships are not affected by buoyancy at all

A reason unrelated to buoyancy

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights outlines fundamental rights meant to be protected for all people, and Canada upholds many of these rights through its own laws and protections.

quiz.q: Why is it valuable for students to learn about human rights?
options: Human rights have no connection to understanding society

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Analyzing Memes and Internet Culture
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: memes use images, text, and humour to quickly spread ideas online, and analyzing them involves considering their intended message, audience, and potential impact.

quiz.q: A meme typically combines ___.
options: A concept unrelated to memes

quiz.q: Why can memes spread ideas quickly online?
options: Memes are always difficult to understand quickly
Memes cannot be shared online

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Algebra: Solving Equations Involving Fractions and Decimals

subjects.subject: Science

subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: an invasive species is a non-native organism introduced to an ecosystem, often causing harm by outcompeting native species for resources.

options: A method unrelated to species introduction

quiz.q: Why can invasive species be especially difficult to control once established?

A reason unrelated to invasive species

quiz.q: Why do scientists study the impact of invasive species on ecosystems?
options: Invasive species have no real impact on ecosystems worth studying

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: Canada’s electoral system allows citizens to vote for representatives in federal, provincial, and municipal elections, playing a key role in how government leaders are chosen.

quiz.q: Why might it be important for citizens to understand the voting process before an election?

subjects.subject: Language

subjects.subject: Math

subjects.subject: Science

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

subjects.subject: Language

In contrast

quiz.q: Which phrase could signal a contrast between two ideas?

In addition
Similarly
A phrase unrelated to signalling contrast

quiz.q: Which phrase could be used to add a similar or additional idea?

In addition
However

quiz.q: Why might a writer use transitional phrases throughout an essay?
options: Transitional phrases always make an essay harder to follow

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Financial Literacy: Income, Expenses, and Net Worth
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: net worth is calculated by subtracting total expenses or debts from total income or assets, helping individuals understand and track their overall financial position.

quiz.q: Net worth is calculated by ___.
options: A concept unrelated to net worth
Subtracting total debts from total assets

Adding income and expenses together

quiz.q: Income refers to ___.
options: Money spent on goods and services
A type of debt owed to a bank
Money earned or received, such as from a job
A concept unrelated to income

quiz.q: Expenses refer to ___.
options: Money spent on goods, services, or bills
A type of savings account
A concept unrelated to expenses
Money earned from working

quiz.q: If a person has $5,000 in assets and $2,000 in debts, what is their net worth?
options: A value unrelated to the calculation

quiz.q: Why is tracking income and expenses important for financial literacy?
options: Net worth has no connection to income or expenses
It helps individuals understand their financial position and make informed spending decisions
A reason unrelated to financial literacy
Tracking income and expenses provides no useful financial information

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Groundwater and the Water Table
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: groundwater is water stored beneath the Earth’s surface in soil and rock, and the water table marks the upper boundary of the area saturated with this water.

quiz.q: Groundwater is water that is stored ___.
options: In clouds high in the atmosphere
A concept unrelated to groundwater
Only on the surface of oceans and lakes
Beneath the Earth’s surface, in soil and rock

quiz.q: The water table marks ___.
options: A concept unrelated to the water table
The boundary between two oceans
The exact centre of the Earth
The upper boundary of the area saturated with groundwater

quiz.q: Which of these could cause the water table to drop?
options: A cause unrelated to the water table
A significant increase in annual rainfall
Excessive pumping of groundwater for human use
A process unrelated to groundwater levels

quiz.q: A well is typically drilled deep enough to reach ___.
options: Only the very surface of the soil
A concept unrelated to wells
A location with no connection to groundwater
Below the water table, where groundwater is present

quiz.q: Why is groundwater an important resource to protect from pollution?
options: Groundwater has no connection to drinking water supplies
A reason unrelated to groundwater
Pollution never affects groundwater quality
Many communities rely on it as a source of drinking water

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Urban vs. Rural Life in Canada
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: urban areas are densely populated with access to many services, while rural areas have lower population density and often rely more on agriculture or natural resources, creating distinct lifestyles across Canada.

quiz.q: Urban areas are generally characterized by ___.
options: Very low populations with few services
A complete absence of any people
Dense populations and many available services
A concept unrelated to urban areas

quiz.q: Rural areas often rely more heavily on ___.
options: Only large corporate offices
A concept unrelated to rural economies
Agriculture or natural resources
A resource unrelated to rural economies

quiz.q: Which of these might be a challenge faced by people living in rural areas?
options: A challenge unrelated to rural areas
Longer travel distances to access certain services
An overwhelming number of nearby services
No connection to distance or access at all

quiz.q: Which of these might be a challenge faced by people living in urban areas?
options: No population at all
Higher cost of living and traffic congestion
A complete absence of any nearby services
A challenge unrelated to urban areas

quiz.q: Why is it useful to compare urban and rural life in Canada?
options: Comparing these areas has no relevance to social studies
Urban and rural life are always identical in every way
A reason unrelated to social studies learning

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Reading: Evaluating an Author’s Credentials and Expertise
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: evaluating an author’s credentials and expertise involves considering their background, training, and experience to judge how reliable their claims about a topic might be.

quiz.q: An author’s credentials refer to their ___.
options: A concept unrelated to author credentials
Background, training, and experience related to a topic
Physical appearance
Favourite hobbies with no connection to the topic

quiz.q: Why might a reader check an author’s expertise before trusting their claims?
options: A reason unrelated to evaluating sources
An author’s background never affects how reliable their claims are
Expertise can indicate how reliable and well-informed the author’s claims are likely to be
All authors are equally reliable regardless of expertise

quiz.q: Which is an example of a credential that might support an author’s expertise on a medical topic?
options: A hobby unrelated to medicine
A concept unrelated to medical expertise
Years of experience working as a doctor
No connection to the medical field at all

quiz.q: Why might a text written by someone with no relevant expertise be viewed with more caution?
options: The claims may be less informed or less reliable without proper background knowledge
Expertise never matters when evaluating a text
A reason unrelated to evaluating a text
A lack of expertise always makes a text more trustworthy

quiz.q: Why is evaluating an author’s credentials an important reading skill?
options: It helps readers judge how much trust to place in a text’s claims
This skill has no effect on understanding a text
A reason unrelated to reading comprehension
Every author’s claims should be trusted equally without question

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Geometry: Constructing Triangles and Angle Bisectors
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: triangles can be constructed using given side lengths or angles, and an angle bisector is a line that divides an angle into two equal parts.

quiz.q: An angle bisector divides an angle into ___.
options: Four unequal parts
A concept unrelated to angle bisectors
Three equal parts
Two equal parts

quiz.q: To construct a triangle given three side lengths, a compass is often used to ___.
options: Draw a circle unrelated to the triangle
A concept unrelated to triangle construction
Measure the temperature of the triangle
Mark equal distances from given points

quiz.q: If an angle measures 60 degrees, its bisector creates two angles of ___ each.
options: 60 degrees
15 degrees

options: 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm

quiz.q: Why might construction tools like a compass and straightedge be used in geometry?
options: These tools never help with accuracy in geometry
A reason unrelated to geometric construction
Constructions can always be done more accurately by estimating

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Integumentary System: Skin, Hair, and Nails
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: the integumentary system, made up of the skin, hair, and nails, protects the body from injury and infection while helping regulate body temperature.

quiz.q: The integumentary system is made up of the skin, hair, and ___.
options: Nails
Blood vessels only
A structure unrelated to the integumentary system
Bones

quiz.q: One main function of the skin is to ___.
options: A function unrelated to the skin
Pump blood throughout the body
Protect the body from injury and infection

quiz.q: The skin helps regulate body temperature through processes such as ___.
options: Digesting food
A process unrelated to temperature regulation
Filtering air for the lungs
Sweating

quiz.q: Which of these is a function of hair on the human body?
options: Providing some protection and insulation

quiz.q: Why is the integumentary system considered the body’s first line of defence?
options: A reason unrelated to the integumentary system

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Canada’s Mining and Natural Resource Industries
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: Canada’s mining and natural resource industries extract valuable materials like minerals and metals, playing a significant role in the economy while raising important questions about environmental impact.

quiz.q: Canada’s mining industry primarily focuses on extracting ___.
options: Minerals and metals
A concept unrelated to mining
Only water resources
A resource unrelated to mining

quiz.q: Why are mining and natural resource industries significant to Canada’s economy?
options: These industries provide no economic benefit at all
They have no connection to Canada’s economy
They provide jobs and generate significant economic activity
A reason unrelated to Canada’s economy

quiz.q: Which of these is a potential environmental concern related to mining?
options: A concern unrelated to mining
Mining always improves the surrounding environment
Disruption of ecosystems and habitats near mining sites

quiz.q: Why might governments regulate mining and resource extraction?
options: A reason unrelated to resource regulation

quiz.q: Why is it useful for students to learn about Canada’s natural resource industries?
options: Natural resource industries have no connection to understanding Canada

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Review: Language Skills (Days 61-69)
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: this review lesson revisits key ideas from Days 61-69, including author’s purpose, business letters, run-on sentences, homophones, conflict, memes, PSAs, transitions, and author credibility.

subjects.subject: Math

options: A value unrelated to the calculation

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Review: Science Skills (Days 61-69)
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: this review lesson revisits key ideas from Days 61-69, including the nervous system, volcanoes and earthquakes, magnetism, the greenhouse effect, and biotechnology.

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

subjects.subject: Language

subjects.subject: Math

quiz.q: What did Britain ask of Canada during the Chanak Crisis?
options: Financial aid for a railway
Military support in a conflict near Turkey
Support for a trade agreement
Help building a new capital city

quiz.q: When did the Chanak Crisis occur?
How did Canada respond to Britains request during the Chanak Crisis?
options: Canada declared war on Britain
Canada immediately sent troops with no debate
Canada ignored the request entirely with no response

quiz.q: Why is the Chanak Crisis considered important in Canadian history?
options: It occurred after Canada already had full independence
It was an early step toward greater Canadian independence in foreign affairs
It ended all ties between Canada and Britain
It had no lasting impact on Canada

options: The Klondike Gold Rush
The Statute of Westminster

subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: a loanword is a word borrowed from another language and adopted into everyday use, such as ballet from French or tsunami from Japanese.

options: A word borrowed from another language and adopted into common use

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Data Management: Weighted Averages
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: a weighted average gives different values different levels of importance before averaging, used when some data points should count more than others, such as test scores worth different percentages.

quiz.q: What does a weighted average take into account that a regular average does not?
options: Only the largest value in a data set
Different levels of importance for different values
Only the smallest value in a data set
Nothing different from a regular average

options: Only when there is a single data point

options: A weighted average calculation
An irrelevant piece of information

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Coral Reefs and Ocean Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: coral reefs are diverse underwater ecosystems built by tiny coral organisms, providing habitat for countless marine species while being sensitive to changes in ocean temperature and acidity.

Rising ocean temperature and increased acidity

options: A process that makes coral healthier
A type of coral reproduction
A stress response where coral loses its colour and often dies without recovery

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

Mining
Agriculture

Only modern technology

subjects.title: Math Review: Geometry, Measurement, and Data

subjects.subject: Language

subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: a collective noun names a group treated as a single unit, such as team, class, or family, and it typically takes a singular verb unless the individual members are clearly acting separately.

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Probability: Conditional Probability (Intro)
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: conditional probability is the probability that an event happens given that another event has already occurred, and it often differs from the probability of that event occurring on its own.

options: The probability of an event that can never happen
A concept unrelated to probability
The probability of two events that are always identical

quiz.q: If a bag has 3 red and 2 blue marbles and one red marble is removed without replacement, how does the probability of drawing another red marble change?
options: It increases to 100 percent automatically
It decreases, since one red marble and one total marble were removed
It stays exactly the same as before
A concept unrelated to probability

The probability of A multiplied by B with no condition
The probability of A occurring before B is defined

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Solutions, Solubility, and Concentration
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: a solution forms when one substance dissolves evenly into another, solubility describes how much of a substance can dissolve in a given amount of solvent, and concentration describes how much solute is present in a solution.

quiz.q: What is a solution?

quiz.q: What does solubility describe?
options: A concept unrelated to solubility
The colour of a substance only
The temperature at which a substance freezes
How much of a substance can dissolve in a given amount of solvent

quiz.q: What does concentration describe in a solution?
options: A concept unrelated to solutions
How much solute is present in a solution
The exact colour of the solvent

quiz.q: Why might sugar dissolve faster in hot water than in cold water?
options: Cold water always dissolves sugar faster than hot water

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

options: A concept unrelated to Canadian history
Colonists who fought for American independence
A group of French explorers who settled Quebec
Colonists who remained loyal to Britain during the American Revolution

quiz.q: Where did many United Empire Loyalists resettle after the American Revolution?

A concept unrelated to Loyalist settlement

quiz.q: Why did United Empire Loyalists leave the newly independent United States?

A concept unrelated to Canadian history
They wished to remain under British rule rather than live in the new republic

quiz.q: How did the arrival of United Empire Loyalists affect the population of British North America?

The item is destroyed and cannot be replaced
The item is doubled before the next draw

quiz.q: How do probabilities change across draws in a without replacement scenario?
options: They always stay exactly the same
They change because the total number of items decreases

By having no effect on the land at all

options: A concept unrelated to glaciers

It turns instantly into solid rock
It disappears completely with no trace left behind

options: Some Canadians wanted to preserve stronger visual ties to British symbols like the Red Ensign
The debate had no connection to Canadian identity or history
This concept has no relevance to social studies
Every Canadian agreed completely on the new design from the start

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Evaluating Influencer Marketing
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: influencer marketing happens when a social media personality promotes a product, often for payment, and viewers benefit from recognizing sponsored content and thinking critically about whether a recommendation is genuine.

quiz.q: What is influencer marketing?
options: A concept unrelated to media literacy
A completely unpaid recommendation with no business relationship
A type of printed magazine advertisement only
When a social media personality promotes a product, often for payment

quiz.q: Why are influencers often required to disclose when content is sponsored?
options: A concept unrelated to influencer marketing
Sponsored content is always identical to genuine, unpaid opinions
So viewers know a payment or partnership may have influenced the recommendation
Disclosure is never required for sponsored content

quiz.q: Why is it important to think critically about an influencers product recommendation?
options: Critical thinking is never useful when viewing social media content
Every influencer recommendation is always completely unbiased
The recommendation may be influenced by payment rather than the influencers honest opinion
A concept unrelated to media literacy

quiz.q: Which of these might indicate a social media post is sponsored content?
options: A post that never mentions a brand or product at all
A concept unrelated to influencer marketing
A post with absolutely no connection to any product
A label such as ad or sponsored included in the post

quiz.q: Why does influencer marketing matter to consumers making purchasing decisions?
options: This concept has no relevance to media literacy
Sponsored content has no effect on what consumers decide to buy
Recognizing sponsored content helps consumers make more informed choices
Consumers can never be influenced by social media content

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Geometry: Tessellations and Symmetry
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: a tessellation is a repeating pattern of shapes that covers a flat surface with no gaps or overlaps, and shapes like equilateral triangles, squares, and regular hexagons can tessellate because their angles divide evenly around a point.

quiz.q: What is a tessellation?
options: A concept unrelated to geometry
A single shape that never repeats in any pattern
A repeating pattern of shapes that covers a surface with no gaps or overlaps
A pattern that always leaves large gaps between shapes

quiz.q: Which of these regular shapes can tessellate on its own?
options: A square
A regular pentagon
A regular heptagon
A concept unrelated to tessellations

quiz.q: Why can a regular hexagon tessellate without leaving any gaps?
options: A concept unrelated to tessellations
Its interior angles divide evenly into 360 degrees around each point
Its interior angles always add up to more than 360 degrees
Hexagons can never fit together without leaving gaps

quiz.q: What role does symmetry often play in a tessellating pattern?
options: Tessellations can never contain any symmetry at all
A concept unrelated to geometry
Symmetry always prevents shapes from tessellating
It helps the repeating shapes align consistently across the surface

quiz.q: Which natural structure is often cited as an example of a tessellating pattern?
options: A honeycomb made of hexagonal cells
A concept unrelated to tessellations
A cloud with no repeating shape
A single round pebble

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Nanotechnology: Engineering at the Atomic Scale
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: nanotechnology involves designing and manipulating materials at an extremely small scale, measured in nanometres, enabling applications such as targeted drug delivery in medicine and stronger, lighter materials in engineering.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

quiz.q: What is nanotechnology?
options: The design and manipulation of materials at an extremely small, nanometre scale
The study of objects that are visible only from space
A concept unrelated to science
A technology that only works on objects larger than a house

quiz.q: Roughly how small is a nanometre?
options: About one billionth of a metre
About one metre exactly
A concept unrelated to nanotechnology
About one thousand kilometres

quiz.q: Why might materials behave differently at the nanoscale compared to their normal, everyday size?
options: Extremely small particles can have different physical and chemical properties than larger amounts of the same material
Nanoscale materials never have any special properties
A concept unrelated to nanotechnology
Materials always behave in exactly the same way no matter their size

quiz.q: How is nanotechnology sometimes used in medicine?
options: To help deliver medication directly and precisely to targeted cells
Nanotechnology has no applications in medicine at all
This concept has no connection to science
To completely replace the need for any medical treatment

quiz.q: Why might engineers use nanotechnology to develop new materials?
options: This concept has no relevance to science
New materials can never be developed using nanotechnology
It can help create materials that are stronger or lighter than traditional materials
Nanotechnology can only make materials heavier and weaker

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: Canadas Peacekeeping Mission in Cyprus
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: Canada contributed troops to a United Nations peacekeeping force in Cyprus beginning in 1964 to help maintain a ceasefire between Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, becoming one of Canadas longest peacekeeping commitments.

quiz.q: What was the purpose of the United Nations peacekeeping force sent to Cyprus?
options: A concept unrelated to Canadian history
To help maintain a ceasefire between Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities
To build new highways across the island
To conquer new territory on behalf of the United Nations

quiz.q: Why was a peacekeeping force needed in Cyprus in the 1960s?
options: Cyprus had no history of any internal tension at all
A concept unrelated to peacekeeping
The mission was sent for reasons unrelated to any conflict
Tension and conflict existed between the islands two main ethnic communities

quiz.q: Roughly how long did Canadian troops contribute to the peacekeeping mission in Cyprus?
options: Canada never sent any troops to Cyprus
Several decades
Only a single afternoon
A concept unrelated to Cyprus

quiz.q: What is the general goal of a peacekeeping mission like the one in Cyprus?
options: A concept unrelated to peacekeeping
To maintain a ceasefire and help prevent renewed violence
To take direct military control of the region permanently
To end all communication between the two communities involved

quiz.q: Why did missions like the one in Cyprus contribute to Canadas international reputation?
options: Canada has never participated in any peacekeeping mission
This concept has no relevance to social studies
Peacekeeping missions have no connection to how other countries view Canada
They reinforced Canadas identity as a committed contributor to international peacekeeping efforts

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Grammar: Reported (Indirect) Speech
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: reported speech restates what someone said without using their exact words in quotation marks, often shifting the verb tense and changing pronouns to fit the perspective of the person reporting it.

quiz.q: What is reported speech?
options: A word-for-word quotation placed in quotation marks
A sentence with no connection to speech at all
Restating what someone said without using their exact quoted words
A concept unrelated to grammar

quiz.q: If someone says I am tired, how might this be rewritten in reported speech?
options: She said tired I am.
A concept unrelated to reported speech
She said I am tired.
She said she was tired.

quiz.q: Why does the verb tense often shift when converting direct speech into reported speech?
options: Reported speech always uses the future tense regardless of the original statement
A concept unrelated to grammar
Reported speech usually moves the tense back to reflect that the statement happened earlier
Verb tense never changes when converting to reported speech

quiz.q: Why might pronouns change when converting direct speech into reported speech?
options: The pronouns need to match the perspective of the person reporting the statement
Reported speech always removes every pronoun completely
This concept has no connection to grammar
Pronouns are never affected by converting speech into reported form

quiz.q: Which sentence is written correctly in reported speech?
options: He said that will call later he.
He said, He would call later.
He said that I will call later.
He said that he would call later.

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Measurement: Converting Units of Area and Volume
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: converting between units of area requires squaring the linear conversion factor, while converting between units of volume requires cubing it, since area and volume involve two and three dimensions respectively.

quiz.q: Why must a linear conversion factor be squared when converting between units of area?
options: A concept unrelated to measurement
Squaring a conversion factor only applies to units of volume
Because area involves two dimensions, so the conversion factor applies twice
Area conversions never require any adjustment to the linear factor

quiz.q: How many square centimetres are in 1 square metre, given 100 centimetres in 1 metre?
Why must a linear conversion factor be cubed when converting between units of volume?
options: Because volume involves three dimensions, so the conversion factor applies three times
A concept unrelated to measurement
Cubing a conversion factor only applies to units of area
Volume conversions never require any adjustment to the linear factor

quiz.q: How many cubic centimetres are in 1 cubic metre, given 100 centimetres in 1 metre?
Why can the simple linear conversion factor not be used directly when converting square or cubic units?
options: Linear, square, and cubic units always convert using the exact same factor
This concept has no connection to measurement
Square and cubic units never need any conversion at all
Applying it without squaring or cubing would ignore the extra dimensions involved

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Circadian Rhythms and the Sleep-Wake Cycle
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: a circadian rhythm is an internal biological clock that repeats roughly every 24 hours, regulating the sleep-wake cycle and other body functions largely in response to patterns of light and darkness.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

quiz.q: What is a circadian rhythm?
options: A pattern found only in plants, never in animals
A concept unrelated to biology
A rhythm that only occurs once per year
An internal biological clock that repeats roughly every 24 hours

quiz.q: What is one major factor that helps regulate the circadian rhythm?
options: A concept unrelated to circadian rhythms
The number of books a person owns
The colour of a persons clothing
Exposure to light and darkness

quiz.q: Why is a consistent sleep-wake cycle generally considered important for the body?
options: It supports healthy brain function, mood, and overall physical health
The body functions identically whether or not a person sleeps
A concept unrelated to biology
Sleep has no measurable effect on the brain or body

quiz.q: What might disrupt a persons circadian rhythm?
options: Waking up at the exact same time every single day
Exposure to bright screen light late at night
A completely dark, quiet room used only for sleeping
A concept unrelated to circadian rhythms

quiz.q: Why might travelling across many time zones cause jet lag?
options: Jet lag has no connection to the circadian rhythm at all
The circadian rhythm instantly resets the moment a plane lands
It temporarily disrupts the bodys internal clock, which has not yet adjusted to the new light pattern
This concept has no relevance to science

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: The National Energy Program and Western Alienation
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: the National Energy Program, introduced by the federal government in 1980, aimed to increase Canadian control over the oil industry and stabilize energy prices, but it angered many in western provinces like Alberta and deepened feelings of western alienation.

quiz.q: What was the National Energy Program?
options: A federal policy from 1980 aimed at increasing Canadian control over oil and stabilizing prices
An agreement to import all of Canadas oil from other countries
A program focused entirely on building new schools
A concept unrelated to Canadian history

quiz.q: Why did the federal government introduce the National Energy Program?
options: To eliminate the energy industry from the Canadian economy entirely
To transfer full control of oil resources to another country
To increase Canadian ownership of the energy industry and manage energy prices
A concept unrelated to the National Energy Program

quiz.q: How did many people in western provinces, especially Alberta, react to the National Energy Program?
options: They were completely unaffected by the policy
A concept unrelated to western Canada
With enthusiastic support and no objections at all
With anger, feeling the policy unfairly targeted their regions oil industry

quiz.q: What does the term western alienation generally describe?
options: A feeling among people in western Canada that the federal government overlooks or mistreats their interests
A term with no connection to any Canadian region
A concept unrelated to Canadian politics
A feeling of strong satisfaction with federal government policies

quiz.q: Why is the National Energy Program still discussed in relation to regional tensions in Canada?
options: This concept has no relevance to social studies
It has been completely forgotten and has no lasting significance
It only affected a single small town with no wider impact
It is often cited as a key example of conflict between federal policy and western provincial interests

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Vocabulary: Acronyms and Initialisms
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: an acronym is an abbreviation formed from the first letters of a phrase and pronounced as a single word, such as NASA, while an initialism is pronounced letter by letter, such as FBI.

quiz.q: What is an acronym?
options: An abbreviation formed from initial letters and pronounced as a single word
A concept unrelated to vocabulary
A word with no connection to any longer phrase
A phrase that is always written out in full with no shortening

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of an acronym pronounced as a word?
options: FBI
NASA
ATM
CD

quiz.q: How does an initialism differ from an acronym?
options: An initialism and an acronym are always pronounced in exactly the same way
An initialism can never be formed from a phrase
An initialism is pronounced letter by letter rather than as a single word
A concept unrelated to vocabulary

quiz.q: Why might people use acronyms and initialisms in everyday language?
options: Acronyms and initialisms always make communication more confusing with no benefit
They shorten long phrases into something quicker and easier to say
This concept has no connection to vocabulary

quiz.q: Which of these is best described as an initialism rather than an acronym?
options: A word that has no letters at all
FBI, pronounced letter by letter
NASA, pronounced as a single word
A concept unrelated to abbreviations

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Probability: Geometric Probability with Area Models
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: geometric probability compares the area of a favourable region to the area of the entire possible region, useful for situations like a dart landing inside a target or a spinner stopping in a certain zone.

quiz.q: What does geometric probability compare?
options: The number of dice rolled in an experiment
The exact colour of a spinner with no connection to area
A concept unrelated to probability
The area of a favourable region to the area of the entire possible region

quiz.q: If a target has a total area of 100 square centimetres and a bullseye area of 20 square centimetres, what is the probability of landing in the bullseye?
options: 20 out of 100
20 out of 80
100 out of 20
80 out of 100

quiz.q: How does geometric probability differ from counting individual equally likely outcomes?
options: Geometric probability can never be applied to a spinner or dartboard
Geometric probability and counting outcomes are always calculated in exactly the same way

A concept unrelated to probability

options: Smaller regions always have a higher probability than larger ones
A larger area typically represents a greater share of the total possible outcomes
This concept has no connection to probability

quiz.q: Why are area models especially useful for probability situations involving continuous space, like a dartboard?
options: They allow probability to be calculated using regions rather than only countable, separate outcomes

This concept has no relevance to math

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: The Doppler Effect and Changing Sound
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: the Doppler effect is the change in pitch heard when a sound source moves relative to a listener, with pitch rising as the source approaches and falling as it moves away, caused by sound waves being compressed or stretched.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

quiz.q: What is the Doppler effect?
options: A change in the colour of an object as it moves
A sound that never changes no matter how it moves
A concept unrelated to science
A change in pitch caused by relative motion between a sound source and a listener

quiz.q: What happens to the pitch of a siren as an ambulance approaches, then passes by?
options: The pitch sounds higher while approaching and lower after it passes
The pitch always stays exactly the same the entire time
A concept unrelated to the Doppler effect
The pitch becomes silent the moment the ambulance passes

quiz.q: What causes sound waves to seem compressed as a source moves toward a listener?
options: Compression only happens when a sound source is standing still
Sound waves always spread out further as a source approaches
A concept unrelated to sound
The source is catching up slightly to its own previously emitted sound waves

quiz.q: Why does pitch sound lower as a sound source moves away from a listener?
options: This concept has no connection to science
The sound waves are compressed further as the source moves away
Pitch never changes based on the motion of a sound source

quiz.q: Which field uses the Doppler effect to help detect the speed and direction of moving objects?
options: Handwriting analysis
Basic arithmetic
Weather radar

subjects.subject: SocialStudies

subjects.subject: Language

options: A character who is always purely good with no flaws

A total absence of personality or motivation

options: An anti-hero and a villain are always exactly the same role in a story

A character who never appears in the story at all

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Algebra: Solving Word Problems with Consecutive Integers
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: consecutive integers are whole numbers that follow each other in order, such as 5, 6, and 7, and word problems about them can be solved by representing the unknown integers algebraically as n, n+1, n+2, and so on.

Numbers that are always separated by a gap of at least ten

options: It turns a wordy description into a solvable equation with a single unknown
Algebra can never be used to represent consecutive integers
This concept has no connection to math

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Renewable Energy: Hydrogen Fuel Cells
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: a hydrogen fuel cell generates electricity through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen, producing water as its main byproduct, making it a clean energy option though challenges remain around storing and producing hydrogen.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

options: Burning coal in a large furnace

options: A concept unrelated to hydrogen fuel cells

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: The History of O Canada and National Symbols
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: O Canada was composed in 1880 and became Canadas official national anthem in 1980, joining other national symbols like the Maple Leaf flag as a shared marker of Canadian identity.

subjects.subject: Language

subjects.subject: Math

subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: indirect measurement uses similar triangles, such as the triangles formed by an object and its shadow, to calculate a height or distance that would be difficult to measure directly, by setting up a proportion between corresponding sides.

options: A method that always requires physically climbing to the top of an object
A method that can only be used on objects smaller than one metre

quiz.q: What is a literary archetype?

A recurring character type or pattern found across many stories
A type of punctuation used in dialogue

quiz.q: What should a podcast script generally include?
options: A list of unrelated topics with no connections between them
A concept unrelated to writing
A strong opening hook, organized segments, and clear transitions
Only a single unbroken paragraph with no structure

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Math Review: Data, Geometry, Financial Literacy, Probability, and Algebra
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand review: students revisit mean absolute deviation, angle relationships in parallel lines, mortgages and amortization, geometric probability, and consecutive integer word problems.

quiz.q: What does mean absolute deviation (MAD) measure?
options: The total number of values in a data set
The single highest value in a data set
The average distance between each data value and the mean
A concept unrelated to data management

quiz.q: What is a transversal?
options: A concept unrelated to geometry
A line that never intersects any other line
A line segment with no defined length
A line that crosses two or more other lines

quiz.q: What is a mortgage?
options: A concept unrelated to financial literacy
A type of savings account with no connection to borrowing
A long-term loan used to purchase property
A one-time payment made in full with no borrowing involved

quiz.q: What does geometric probability compare?
options: The number of dice rolled in an experiment
A concept unrelated to probability
The area of a favourable region to the area of the entire possible region
The exact colour of a spinner with no connection to area

quiz.q: What are consecutive integers?
options: A concept unrelated to algebra
Whole numbers that follow each other in order, such as 5, 6, and 7
Numbers that are always separated by a gap of at least ten
Numbers that must all be equal to each other

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Science Review: Astronomy, Earth Science, Physics, Technology, and Biology
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand review: students revisit comets and asteroids, permafrost and the cryosphere, light and colour, nanotechnology, and circadian rhythms.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

quiz.q: What is a comet mostly made of?
options: A concept unrelated to astronomy
Ice, dust, and rocky material
Solid metal with no ice at all
Pure liquid water only

quiz.q: What is permafrost?
options: Ground that has never once frozen in recorded history
Ground that has remained frozen for two or more consecutive years
A concept unrelated to earth science
A type of rock found only underwater

quiz.q: Why does an object appear a particular colour, such as red?
options: A concept unrelated to science
It reflects that wavelength of light while absorbing most other wavelengths
It creates that colour of light entirely on its own with no outside light needed
Colour has no connection to light at all

quiz.q: What is nanotechnology?
options: A technology that only works on objects larger than a house
A concept unrelated to science
The study of objects that are visible only from space
The design and manipulation of materials at an extremely small, nanometre scale

quiz.q: What is a circadian rhythm?
options: A rhythm that only occurs once per year
An internal biological clock that repeats roughly every 24 hours
A concept unrelated to biology
A pattern found only in plants, never in animals

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies Review: Confederation, Constitution, and Canadian Identity
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand review: students revisit the Fenian Raids, the National Policy of 1879, the patriation of the constitution, the flag debate of 1964, and the history of the CBC.

quiz.q: What were the Fenian Raids?
options: A concept unrelated to Canadian history
A series of scientific expeditions across the Arctic
A series of armed incursions into British North America by an Irish-American group
A peaceful trade negotiation between Canada and Ireland

quiz.q: What was the National Policy of 1879?
options: A policy focused only on education reform
A treaty ending a war between Canada and another country
An economic strategy combining tariffs, a transcontinental railway, and western immigration
A concept unrelated to Canadian history

quiz.q: What does patriation of the constitution mean?
options: A concept unrelated to Canadian history
Sending the constitution to another country for approval
Bringing full authority over the constitution under Canadian control
Removing the constitution from use entirely

quiz.q: What was the Great Canadian Flag Debate of 1964 about?
options: Choosing a new national flag design to replace the existing one
A concept unrelated to Canadian history
Deciding whether Canada should adopt a new national anthem
Choosing the location of a new national capital

quiz.q: What is the CBC?
options: A company that only produces printed newspapers
A publicly funded Canadian broadcaster
A concept unrelated to Canadian history
A privately owned foreign broadcasting company

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Grammar: Modal Verbs and Degrees of Certainty
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: modal verbs such as can, could, may, might, must, and should show degrees of possibility, permission, ability, or obligation, letting a writer express how certain or uncertain a statement is.

quiz.q: What do modal verbs generally express?
options: Degrees of possibility, permission, ability, or obligation
The number of syllables in a sentence
A concept unrelated to grammar
The exact spelling of a word

quiz.q: Which of these words is a modal verb?
options: Quickly
Running
Blue
Must

quiz.q: Which modal verb generally suggests the strongest degree of certainty?
options: May
Might
Must
Could

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose might instead of must in a sentence?
options: A concept unrelated to modal verbs
Might can never be used to express possibility
To show that something is only possible rather than certain
Might and must always mean exactly the same thing

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses a modal verb to show obligation?
options: Assignments Friday must students their by submit.
Students must submit their assignments by Friday.
Friday students by must their submit assignments.
Students submit Friday must assignments their by.

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Algebra: The Slope-Intercept Form of a Linear Equation
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: the slope-intercept form of a linear equation, y = mx + b, describes a straight line using its slope, m, and its y-intercept, b, the point where the line crosses the y-axis.

quiz.q: In the equation y = mx + b, what does m represent?
options: The slope of the line
A concept unrelated to linear equations
The y-intercept of the line
The x-intercept of the line

quiz.q: In the equation y = mx + b, what does b represent?
options: The slope of the line
A concept unrelated to linear equations
The y-intercept of the line
The steepness of the line only

quiz.q: In the equation y = 3x + 5, what is the slope of the line?
In the equation y = 3x + 5, at what point does the line cross the y-axis?
Why is slope-intercept form useful for quickly graphing a line?
options: It never provides any useful information about a line
It directly shows both the steepness and the starting point without extra calculation
It can only be used for lines that pass through the origin
A concept unrelated to graphing

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: Extremophiles: Life in Earths Most Extreme Environments
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: extremophiles are organisms that thrive in conditions once thought too harsh for life, such as boiling hydrothermal vents, highly acidic pools, or extreme cold, expanding scientists understanding of where life can exist.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

quiz.q: What is an extremophile?
options: A concept unrelated to biology
An organism that can only survive in mild, comfortable conditions
A type of rock formed under extreme pressure
An organism that thrives in extremely harsh environmental conditions

quiz.q: Which environment might host extremophiles?
options: A climate-controlled greenhouse only
An environment with absolutely no water or chemicals
Boiling hydrothermal vents on the ocean floor
A concept unrelated to extremophiles

quiz.q: Why do scientists studying the possibility of life on other planets pay close attention to extremophiles?
options: Extremophiles show that life can survive in conditions once thought impossible, widening where life might be found
Extremophiles prove that life can never exist anywhere except Earth
A concept unrelated to astrobiology
Extremophiles have no relevance to the search for life beyond Earth

quiz.q: What is one adaptation that might help an extremophile survive extreme heat?
options: Heat-resistant proteins that do not break down at high temperatures
A concept unrelated to extremophiles
An inability to survive above freezing temperatures
A complete absence of any proteins in its cells

quiz.q: Why might extremophiles be useful in industrial or medical applications?
options: This concept has no connection to science
Their heat- or acid-resistant enzymes can function reliably in harsh industrial processes
Extremophiles have never been used in any industrial or medical application
Extremophile enzymes always stop working outside of a laboratory setting

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: The Durham Report and the Path to Responsible Government
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: after the Rebellions of 1837, Lord Durham was sent to investigate and his 1839 report recommended uniting Upper and Lower Canada and granting responsible government, in which the executive would answer to elected representatives.

quiz.q: Why was Lord Durham sent to British North America in 1838?
options: To investigate the causes of the Rebellions of 1837 and recommend reforms
A concept unrelated to Canadian history
To lead a military campaign against a foreign country
To negotiate a trade agreement with the United States

quiz.q: What did the Durham Report recommend regarding Upper and Lower Canada?
options: Ending all government in both colonies entirely
Uniting them into a single colony
Dividing them into four separate colonies
A concept unrelated to the Durham Report

quiz.q: What does responsible government mean?
options: A government with no elected representatives of any kind
A government controlled entirely by a foreign monarch with no local input
A concept unrelated to Canadian history
The executive branch must answer to and hold the confidence of elected representatives

quiz.q: In what year was the Durham Report presented?
Why is the Durham Report considered an important step toward Confederation?
options: It had no lasting influence on any later political developments
It set in motion political changes that pushed the colonies toward greater self-government
It immediately ended all connection between the colonies and Britain
This concept has no relevance to social studies

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Vocabulary: Jargon and Technical Vocabulary
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: jargon is specialized vocabulary used within a particular profession or field, such as medicine or computer science, that can be precise for insiders but confusing for readers outside that field.

quiz.q: What is jargon?
options: A concept unrelated to vocabulary
A type of punctuation used only in technical writing
Specialized vocabulary used within a particular profession or field
A word that has exactly the same meaning in every possible context

quiz.q: Why might jargon confuse a general audience?
options: It relies on specialized terms that outsiders to the field may not know
General audiences always understand every field of specialized vocabulary
A concept unrelated to jargon
Jargon is always identical to everyday, common vocabulary

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of computer science jargon?
options: Blue
Running
Algorithm
A concept unrelated to vocabulary

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose to avoid heavy jargon when writing for a general audience?
options: To make the writing clear and accessible to readers unfamiliar with the field
General audiences always prefer highly specialized terminology
This concept has no connection to vocabulary
Jargon always makes writing easier for every possible reader to understand

quiz.q: Why might jargon still be useful within a specific professional community?
options: Professional communities always avoid using any specialized terms
Jargon never serves any useful purpose, even among experts
This concept has no relevance to vocabulary
It allows precise, efficient communication among people who share the same specialized knowledge

subjects.subject: Math
subjects.title: Geometry: Inscribed and Circumscribed Circles
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Math strand: an inscribed circle fits perfectly inside a polygon, touching each side exactly once, while a circumscribed circle passes through every vertex of a polygon, surrounding it completely.

quiz.q: What does it mean for a circle to be inscribed in a polygon?
options: The circle has no connection to the polygon at all
The circle passes through every vertex of the polygon
A concept unrelated to geometry
The circle fits inside the polygon and touches each side exactly once

quiz.q: What does it mean for a circle to be circumscribed about a polygon?
options: The circle passes through every vertex of the polygon
The circle fits entirely inside the polygon with no contact to its sides
The circle overlaps only one side of the polygon
A concept unrelated to circumscribed circles

quiz.q: Which circle passes through every vertex of a triangle?
options: A concept unrelated to triangles
The inscribed circle
The circumscribed circle
Neither circle ever touches a vertex

quiz.q: Which circle touches each side of a triangle exactly once?
options: The inscribed circle
A concept unrelated to inscribed circles
The circumscribed circle
Neither circle ever touches a side

quiz.q: Why might architects and designers use inscribed and circumscribed circles when planning circular layouts around polygons?
options: This concept has no relevance to geometry
Inscribed and circumscribed circles have no practical design applications
They help position a circle so it fits precisely inside or around a polygonal shape
These circles can only be drawn around shapes with curved sides

subjects.subject: Science
subjects.title: CRISPR and Modern Gene Editing
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Science strand: CRISPR is a gene-editing tool that allows scientists to precisely cut and modify sections of DNA, opening possibilities for treating genetic diseases, improving crops, and advancing biological research.
subjects.resourceLabel: TVO Learn: Grade 7 Science and Technology

quiz.q: What does CRISPR allow scientists to do?
options: Observe distant galaxies in high resolution
Measure the exact age of a fossil instantly
Precisely cut and modify specific sections of DNA
A concept unrelated to science

quiz.q: Which of these is a potential application of CRISPR technology?
options: A concept unrelated to gene editing
Converting sound waves directly into light
Treating certain genetic diseases
Predicting tomorrows weather with certainty

quiz.q: Why might CRISPR be useful for improving crops?
options: A concept unrelated to CRISPR
It has no possible application in agriculture
It can be used to edit genes that affect traits like drought resistance or yield
It can only be used on animals, never on plants

quiz.q: Why do many scientists consider CRISPR a major advance over earlier gene-editing methods?
options: This concept has no connection to science
It allows far more precise targeting of specific DNA sequences
It is far less precise than every method used before it
CRISPR cannot target any specific section of DNA

quiz.q: Why does CRISPR raise ethical questions among scientists and the public?
options: Editing genes, especially in humans, raises questions about safety and the limits of altering life
This concept has no relevance to science
CRISPR has never been discussed in relation to ethics
Gene editing raises no ethical questions of any kind

subjects.subject: SocialStudies
subjects.title: Social Studies: The Great Coalition and the Charlottetown Conference of 1864
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Social Studies strand: in 1864 political rivals in the Province of Canada formed the Great Coalition to pursue federal union, then met with Maritime delegates at the Charlottetown Conference to begin negotiating the terms that would lead to Confederation in 1867.

quiz.q: What was the Great Coalition of 1864?
options: A treaty signed between Canada and France
A military alliance formed to fight a foreign war
A concept unrelated to Canadian history

quiz.q: What was the original purpose of the Charlottetown Conference?
options: Maritime leaders planned to discuss a union of the Maritime colonies
To negotiate an end to a war with the United States
To formally end all discussion of any colonial union
A concept unrelated to the Charlottetown Conference

quiz.q: Why did delegates from the Province of Canada attend the Charlottetown Conference?
options: They attended purely by accident with no political purpose
To propose a broader union that would eventually include all the colonies
A concept unrelated to Confederation
To formally reject any possibility of future union

quiz.q: In what year did the Charlottetown Conference take place?
Why is the Charlottetown Conference considered a key early step toward Confederation?
options: It had no connection whatsoever to the events of 1867
This concept has no relevance to social studies

subjects.subject: Language
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing Frame Narratives (Stories Within Stories)
subjects.summary: Grade 7 Language strand: a frame narrative is a story that contains another story inside it, using an outer story to introduce, connect, or give context to one or more inner stories told by a character.

A concept unrelated to reading

It has no connection to the inner story at all
